title: One idempotency standard for every REST POST of rwb-source-data
ruling: Every POST requires header Idempotency-Key, a canonical UUID (LDM v10 DF-OPS-185). PLT helper (RWB-PLT-N009) stores the first response in rwb_source_data.idempotency_key with endpoint (method + resolved path) and request_hash (SHA-256 of the body, of the empty string when none); the key is unique within the schema. Missing, blank or non-UUID: 400 MSG-PLT-N009-03. Same key, endpoint and hash: stored status and body replayed (201 stays 201). Different endpoint or hash, or first request in flight: 409 MSG-PLT-N009-05. Store down: 503 MSG-PLT-N009-06. Expiry 24 h (LDM v10 entity idempotency_key). PUT, PATCH and GET carry no key. Business repeats are per operation: rerun 409 (RD-P1-012); retention workflow ID retention-<runDate>-<ruleVersion> with reuse policy ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY; load repeat of the same table, validFrom and hash answers 200 with the first load (RWB-P3-E1043-CON wins over MSG-P1-011); ledger business-key repeat per RD-P1-007. R-UNI-40 counts in processed_event.hit_count (ce_id for events; work key with event_id null for in-process keys); REST replays are not counted. The yaml declares the IdempotencyKey header and 400, 409, 503 on every POST.

title: The error envelope is the published Problem schema, extended once

title: Optimistic concurrency on PUT and PATCH
ruling: A GET of an updatable resource returns header ETag with the row version. Every PUT and PATCH requires If-Match with that version: missing 428 MSG-GEN-004; mismatch 409 MSG-GEN-004 and nothing written. A successful write increments version and returns the new ETag; a PUT whose body equals the stored values writes nothing, keeps the version and answers 200. Applies to PATCH /admin/data-dictionary/fields/{fieldCode}, PATCH /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}, PUT /extension-facts/parties/{personKey} and PUT /extension-facts/accounts/{accountKey}. PUT and PATCH carry no Idempotency-Key; RWB-P1-E1064-APP AC11 is limited to POST /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}/publish.

title: Ledger intake: consumed-event map, identity, filtering, retry and parking, ordering
ruling: All six consumed types carry ce_idempotencykey (business key in the RD-P1-007 form) and ce_actor (USER:, SERVICE: or PARTNER: followed by the identifier); rwb-document and the decision-record library add both headers. actorType = the prefix, actorRef = the rest. Map: sourceSystem WORKBENCH, occurredAt = ce_time, caseId = data.caseId. Row 01 rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1, CASE_CREATED, sourceRef 'EV-01 CaseCreated'. Row 02 rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1, CASE_ALLOCATED, 'EV-02 CaseAllocated', toHolderRef USER:ownerId. Row 03 rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1, CASE_TRANSFERRED, 'EV-04 CaseTransferred', fromHolderRef and toHolderRef USER: plus fromOwner and toOwner. Row 04 rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1, CASE_ESCALATED, 'EV-19 TimerBreached'. Row 05 rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1, DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, 'EV-16 DocumentStored', documentId. Row 06 rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1, DECISION_TAKEN, 'EV-08 DecisionRecorded', decisionLogId = entryId. Other types, and DecisionRecorded without caseId, are committed and ignored; no routing on ce_source; the loop is removed because appends write no decision record. Version = .vN of ce_type; current and previous registered versions accepted (all .v1 now). One transaction: processed_event by ce_id (hit_count + 1 on a repeat), then the in-process append; an existing business key adds no entry. Transient failures retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h, then <topic>.dlt; missing attribute, unsupported version, missing caseId or schema-invalid payload go straight to .dlt with headers rwb-dlt-reason, rwb-dlt-consumer and rwb-dlt-owner; LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED with MSG-P1-022 is raised by the intake only on RETRIES_EXHAUSTED. Non-blocking retry; the ledger is read in occurredAt then caseSeq order. Consumer groups per topic; earliest offset on first start; the feature flag off pauses the consumers.
